about.title: Rancho Cucamonga Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Most people in Rancho Cucamonga never think about who designed the ladder in the garage or the tire on the family SUV until one of them fails. When it does, California law treats the situation differently than an ordinary accident. Under strict product liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You need to show the product had a defect — in its design, in how that particular unit was built, or in the warnings that came with it — and that the defect caused your injury. It also means more than one company may answer for the harm: the maker, the distributor that moved it through San Bernardino County, and the store on Foothill Boulevard that sold it. Some 649 people were injured in Rancho Cucamonga collisions during 2025, and a portion of crashes trace back to an airbag, brake, or seat belt that did not perform as intended. Whatever the product, keep it. We handle these claims on contingency and offer free initial consultations.

whyChoose.title: How We Help With a Defective Product Claim

items.title: Strict Liability Works in Your Favor
items.desc: In most California product cases you do not have to show the manufacturer was negligent. We focus on proving the defect — design, manufacturing, or warning — and tying it to your injury.

items.title: Every Link in the Chain Is Considered
items.desc: The manufacturer, the distributor, and the retailer that sold the item in Rancho Cucamonga may each be responsible. Our team reviews who touched the product on its way to you.

items.title: Guidance on Preserving the Evidence
items.desc: The product itself is usually the heart of the case, so we urge you not to repair, return, or discard it. We can arrange proper storage and testing once you contact us.

items.question: My tire came apart on I-15 near Rancho Cucamonga and I crashed. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. If the tire had a manufacturing or design defect, the tire maker and possibly the seller may be liable under California's strict liability rules, separate from any driver fault. Keep the tire, the wheel, and any purchase records, and avoid letting a shop dispose of them. We can arrange an inspection to see whether a defect played a role.

items.question: Do I have to prove the company was careless?
items.answer: Usually not. California generally applies strict liability to product injuries, so the question is whether the product was defective and whether that defect caused your harm. That said, gathering the right evidence still matters, which is why speaking with us early on is useful.

items.question: The store offered me a refund if I return the product. Should I take it?
items.answer: Be cautious. Returning the item can mean losing the single most important piece of evidence in your claim. Photograph it, store it safely, and talk with us before handing anything over. We handle product liability claims on contingency — you pay nothing unless there is a recovery.
